meta.storyTitle: Design the approved ISSUE-a03e99e17a364550: restore end-to-end historical and runtime-bound daemon source upgrades on qualified macOS/Linux, independently bootstrapping owned Node/npm before native builds and retaining staged activation, trust, rollback and data. Include recovery for partially failed old updates and real historical upgrade qualification.

summary.prose: Restore upgrades from historical and runtime-bound source daemon installations using a current independently delivered bootstrap. Build and native-check the candidate with verified Node/npm before disturbing the incumbent, then activate through the existing macOS owner or a Linux source transaction with durable rollback. Historical clients need a one-time current installer/client delivery; partially failed installations receive explicit diagnosis and a qualified recovery route.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

contractDetails.notes: Existing prepareLegacyUpgrade's inferred internal result is represented as unknown here because s1 located its signature without an explicit return annotation; retain its real completeLegacyMigration return shape in implementation rather than broadening public IPC. All proposed source/journal types are design-only and not assertions of current APIs. Grounding: [[c1]], [[c2]], [[c3]], [[c4]].

dataModelChanges.details: One self-contained current installer/bootstrap is the upgrade authority for newly shipped VS Code/JetBrains, shell ctl, TUI and daemon update helper. Client package generation embeds canonical runtime assets and authenticated source-release bootstrap where that channel requires it. Never run the target's old daemon-ctl update/restart to build it. An old daemon/TUI/client cannot be rewritten in flight: recovery explicitly requires obtaining the newly packaged installer or updating the client, then invoking --migrate-runtime against the existing root; document exact supported distribution/channel and prerequisites. New bootstrap resolves installed selection before routing, preventing fallback to legacy root. Pure stop/start actions retain their owner. Source/managed bundle policies remain distinct.

Private versioned source-lifecycle selector (separate from managed-lifecycle/installation.json) belongs to one canonical state root and maps one stable logical install root to exactly one selected immutable release root and verified runtime binding; records generation, source channel, commit, compatibility identity and prior reference. One selector has zero or one active transaction; each transaction references exactly one candidate and zero or one qualified predecessor. Release/runtime objects may be referenced by multiple retained receipts and are never GC'd here. All Linux shell, IDE, TUI, daemon and MCP/start resolution must consume this selection with schema/ownership/canonical-root validation; an absent selector means legacy behavior, a malformed selector is fatal. Do not overwrite/rename the incumbent checkout or make source runtime binding itself a mutable release selector. Darwin and signed bundle selectors are untouched. No persisted registry/entity/DB relationship changes.

Versioned private journal under source-lifecycle: operation id, state root, old selector or absent sentinel, selected generation, authenticated channel/candidate receipt, prior and candidate pins/runtime references, wasRunning, retained process identity, phase, bounded diagnostic outcome. States reserved -> qualified/staged -> predecessor-exited -> candidate-selected -> candidate-ready -> committed; rollback-required/rolled-back/recovery-required are explicit terminal or recoverable states. One exclusive installation mutation owner serializes update/start/restart during cutover; acquire before capture and recheck at every transition. Reuse existing retained process capability/run-file guard APIs for Linux and kernel-observed exit, not PID age or kill(pid,0). Durable fsync+atomic selector replace with same-filesystem journal checkpoints; unknown fsync/rename outcome must be reread and reconciled before spawn. Recovery never opens live DBs from a client and never releases exclusion while actor closure is unknown.

Inventory independently identifies source HEAD, built output provenance/hash, npm install marker/dependency integrity, runtime binding, live executable/root and dirty tracked/untracked files. Never infer built provenance from current HEAD if out is stale. Dirty source/lockfiles are preserved, diagnosed and never reset/stashed automatically. Normal cutover requires a validated restartable rollback pin plus an authorized compatibility pair for actual prior bytes. Missing/partial node_modules or unverifiable stale output blocks cutover while candidate preparation/diagnostic can proceed. Explicit recovery offers an independently staged last-known-good predecessor from an authenticated qualified commit, or a fresh side-by-side installation when no rollback baseline can be proven; user data remains retained and compatibility-gated. No automatic destructive repair or guessed restart from partial bytes. A running historical daemon can stay running while recovery inputs are prepared. A stopped broken daemon is not described as a working predecessor.

Reuse authenticated source release verifier/catalog and floor semantics before executing candidate npm hooks; factor portable verification/staging from Darwin-only journal admission without replacing macOS owner. Linux source predecessor profiles and compatibility evidence must be explicitly represented and qualified in source-release packaging/verification; do not claim managed/signed Linux bundle support. Missing production signing/bootstrap material fails before incumbent mutation and provides the actual authenticated installer distribution prerequisite, not the current circular migration advice. Candidate source cannot authorize its own compatibility or weaken the verifier. No keys are created/committed by this work. Windows/darwin-x64 remain disabled. Old installs cannot acquire this guarantee through their unchanged updater alone.

errorCases.scenario: Bootstrap/verifier missing, wrong channel, revoked floor or unqualified predecessor
errorCases.detection: Verify delivered source bootstrap, signed receipt/catalog, exact commit, profile and compatibility before candidate npm execution.
errorCases.response: Fail preparation with a concrete current-installer/channel prerequisite; preserve incumbent and receipt floor; never bootstrap from candidate assertions.
errorCases.userImpact: Upgrade withheld; old install remains selected.

errorCases.scenario: Archive/cache corruption or ambient Node/npm injection
errorCases.detection: Digest, private ownership, full runtime inventory and binding checks fail; child probes record unexpected executable/npm identity.
errorCases.response: Reject/re-provision from verified archive using existing runtime owner; no ambient fallback or inventory relaxation.
errorCases.userImpact: No native build/cutover under an unknown runtime.

errorCases.scenario: npm ci, native compilation, build or smoke failure
errorCases.detection: Absolute owned subprocess returns nonzero, times out, or native smoke fails; retain exact command/error and child closure evidence.
errorCases.response: Publish bounded failure diagnostic, retain incumbent selection/data and safe resumable candidate evidence; reap only owned children.
errorCases.userImpact: Working daemon continues; no restart into partial output.

errorCases.scenario: Dirty or partly failed historical install
errorCases.detection: Compare git status, lockfile/install marker, built output provenance, runtime inventory, live process root and exact predecessor pin.
errorCases.response: Preserve all source/lock changes and block cutover until independently staged qualified rollback baseline or explicit side-by-side recovery is admitted.
errorCases.userImpact: Actionable recovery instead of another destructive in-place update.

errorCases.detection: Exclusive reservation/generation comparison and re-read prior pin/selector before each transition detect interference.
errorCases.response: Refuse second mutation; on stale owner use retained incarnation/kernel exit proof and journal recovery, never timestamp-only lock breaking.
errorCases.userImpact: One owner may mutate selection/run files.

errorCases.scenario: Predecessor refuses shutdown or child closure uncertain
errorCases.detection: Retained process capability and kernel-observed exit/run-file guard cannot prove quiescence.
errorCases.response: Keep old selector; withhold candidate start. Invoke existing platform owner stop behavior without adding new PID/IPC fallback logic.
errorCases.userImpact: Upgrade may wait/fail safely; no second daemon opens same stores.

errorCases.detection: Check expected process incarnation, candidate executable/root/commit and daemon health within bounded startup window.
errorCases.response: Prove candidate/children exited, restore exact prior selector or absent sentinel durably, restart qualified prior only if wasRunning. If closure or compatibility unknown remain recovery-required and excluded.
errorCases.userImpact: Rollback if provably safe; otherwise explicit recovery state.

errorCases.scenario: Crash or disk error during journal/selector publication
errorCases.detection: Reopen bounded owned journal, fsync receipts and selector; compare generation, pins and actual actor identities.
errorCases.response: Reconcile idempotently before spawn; uncertain durable state is recovery-required. Never assume rename failure means old selection persisted.
errorCases.userImpact: Retry cannot start both releases or lose rollback reference.

migration.stateBefore: s1 analyzer bundle c1 locates resolveOwnedToolchain/stageManagedRelease/prepareLegacyUpgrade and recovery APIs, shell migration/refusal literals, and incomplete caller/model graph. Direct source checks confirm managed selector/gate are Darwin-only; exact a30aa7f91 old updater invokes ambient npm and existing Linux target is refused. Existing fresh-install native evidence is not historical-upgrade proof.
migration.stateAfter: A newly delivered current bootstrap can stage and qualify a candidate independently of old installed code. macOS uses its existing authenticated lifecycle; qualified Linux source installations use a private durable selection/transaction adapter. Subsequent updates consume selection consistently. Failed historical updates are diagnosed and preserved until qualified recovery is possible.

migrationSteps.action: Deliver current self-contained authenticated source installer through release packaging and current IDE assets, with canonical runtime assets/public verifier and qualified predecessor catalog. The release operator retains signing key custody; implementation must not create a replacement trust root. Document invoking the obtained installer via /bin/bash <current-installer> --target <existing-root> --migrate-runtime with explicit source options. Old clients/TUI/daemon require this one-time external delivery; do not instruct them to rebuild the old install to acquire it.

Inventory incumbent state without modifying it: selector/generation, source channel/HEAD/dirt, output/dependency provenance, live actor/runtime and data compatibility. Record actual old executable identity. Dirty or stale/partial state branches to explicit recovery diagnostics; prepare independent qualified rollback baseline or side-by-side recovery, never reset local edits or infer provenance from current HEAD.

Independently bootstrap verified candidate Node/npm, authenticate exact source/compatibility/predecessor/profile, stage source and native install/build/smoke out of tree; pin prior and candidate runtimes separately and retain references. No live stores or incumbent code/dependencies change. Staged resources are retained or cleaned only after owned-child closure, never while referenced.

Acquire platform mutation admission. Revalidate selector/pins; capture and stop the incumbent through its owner only after staging is complete. Prove original process and relevant children exited and hold run-file exclusion. Persist cutover checkpoint, publish candidate selection durably, then start only if action/previous running state requires it. macOS remains on existing managed cutover; Linux source adapter owns its new selector and recovery journal.

Readiness must identify candidate process/root/commit and health. Commit outcome on success. On failure prove candidate closure before restoring exact prior selector (including absent legacy selection), then restart qualified prior only when it was running and compatibility permits. Unknown closure/state leaves recovery-required and withholds another start.

Qualify historical-to-current and a second update on actual Mac and both OrbStack targets. Ship source-selection consumption to all applicable clients/launchers in the same release, retaining compatibility with absent selectors. Retain incumbent checkout, data and runtime receipts; this work performs no GC.

migration.backwardCompat: Existing daemon IPC methods/result payloads remain compatible; update launch acknowledgments remain distinct from final outcomes. Existing signed macOS managed installation schema, supervisor and bundle policy stay authoritative. Linux selector is additive and absent means legacy routing; malformed means explicit failure. New clients resolve selected release before start/MCP/update. An unchanged old binary is not guaranteed to understand new selection: route it through one-time installer/client update and document that legacy launchers must not start retained roots directly after migration. Update versus restart running-state semantics must remain explicit. No Windows support, deprecated fork work or new IPC-stop fallback.

alternativesConsidered.name: Independent bootstrap with staged source transactions
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Deliver the current bootstrap outside the incumbent, share owned-runtime staging, and keep activation with each platform's lifecycle owner.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New clients and a newly delivered self-contained installer invoke the same current upgrade bootstrap rather than old ctl update functions. Preserve macOS authenticated managed migration/update and add a Linux source installation selector plus durable source transaction adapter around existing verified staging/runtime APIs. Keep signed bundle and source authority distinct; never turn off signature gates to accommodate raw installers.
pros: Smallest shape meeting both historical reachability and qualified platform upgrades.
Reuses owned Node/npm, candidate pinning/native qualification and macOS owner.
Allows a subsequent update and recovery without rebuilding the incumbent.
cons: Needs explicit Linux source selector and recovery protocol because managed selector is Darwin-only.
Old clients require a one-time new installer or client delivery.
Historical dirty/stale installations can require explicit recovery admission.

alternativesConsidered.name: Extend the macOS managed supervisor to Linux
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use one platform-neutral supervisor/selector for every installation.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Generalize the current Darwin incarnation, launchctl job, managed mutation gate and recovery contracts into platform-neutral services, then route all upgrades through the expanded supervisor.
cons: Reworks unrelated supervisor and launch-service architecture.
Much larger safety qualification surface than the existing-install defect requires.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Satisfies acceptance only by redesigning unrelated platform supervisor contracts; a1 reuses existing macOS authority with less scope.

alternativesConsidered.name: Deliver only a runtime-prefixed legacy updater
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Prefix Node/npm and native environment around old installed scripts.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New launchers provision Node/npm and export their environment before invoking old ctl update. Keep old in-place git/npm behavior and existing-target installer refusal.
pros: Small routing change addresses bare npm selection in some old scripts.
cons: Fails runtime-bound source updates and Linux staged migration acceptance.
In-place source/dependency mutations cannot preserve a validated rollback predecessor.
Old clients still cannot obtain bootstrap behavior automatically.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fails qualified staged migration, data/rollback preservation, partial-update recovery and historical upgrade proof; runtime prefix alone is insufficient.

erDefinition.narrative: Shows installation selection and rollback retention ownership; platform cutover remains separate from immutable runtime verification. Each installation has at most one active transaction, and both candidate and prior pins retain their own runtime.

SourceInstallation.description: Linux source installation selection owned by one canonical state root; macOS keeps its existing selector.

selected.description: Exactly one selected release after migration.

activeTransaction.description: At most one exclusive source upgrade transaction.

UpgradeTransaction.description: Durable operation journal retained until committed or safely rolled back.

prior.description: Qualified rollback release; absent only before legacy admission/recovery.

phase.description: Durable preparation, cutover or recovery state.

ReleasePin.description: Immutable release bytes plus separately retained verified runtime.

fingerprint.description: Measured built bytes retained for revalidation.

runtime.description: Exact verified runtime independently retained per release.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Shows independent bootstrap delivery, preparation before disruption, and platform-owned activation. Failure before cutover leaves the incumbent running; rollback after selection requires proof of candidate exit.
